cases.name: inert-patch
cases.covers: A patch that repeats what is already there. Nothing changed value, so the appearance is preserved and a client is told not to re-raster.

cases.name: metadata-only
cases.covers: Contents and flags, neither of which is painted on a highlight. Still inert, which is what stops editing a comment from destroying a shape.

cases.name: colour-change
cases.covers: A semantic edit. The appearance is re-baked and the client is told so.

cases.name: quad-translation
cases.covers: A text markup whose quads all move by one delta, which re-bakes rather than preserving. A markup's /Rect is DERIVED from its quads rather than patched, so the patch carries no rect, and the rigid-translation check requires one: it has no way to know the box moved with them. The shape family, whose rect IS the patch, takes the other road.

cases.name: quad-growth
cases.covers: A second quad added to a one-quad markup. PDFium can grow the list and not shrink it, so this is the direction that works, and /Rect has to enclose both afterwards.

cases.name: clearing-contents
cases.covers: A tri-state clear of a value that was there. This is where writing an empty string instead of removing the key becomes visible: the read side reports absent and empty differently.

cases.name: flags-preserve-what-they-do-not-mention
cases.covers: The annotation is created printing and the patch hides it. Hiding must not also stop it printing.

cases.name: square-rect-translation
cases.covers: A shape moved without resizing, which DOES preserve: the patch carries the rect, so the translation can be verified. Read beside quad-translation, which cannot be.

cases.name: square-resize
cases.covers: A shape resized. The pixels would be scaled rather than shifted, so it re-bakes.

cases.name: square-border-width-only
cases.covers: A width with no style. /BS is one native call taking both, so the style has to be read rather than defaulted, or a patch that never mentioned it would reset it.

cases.name: square-clear-interior
cases.covers: A tri-state clear of a fill that was there.

cases.name: square-clear-cloudy
cases.covers: A tri-state clear of a cloudy border that was there.

cases.name: strikeout-intent
cases.covers: The /IT a strikeout can carry, set by a patch rather than at creation.

cases.name: polygon-fewer-vertices
cases.covers: A vertex list that SHRINKS, which /QuadPoints cannot do. SetVertices replaces the array rather than appending to it, so there is no stale tail and no preflight to refuse one.

cases.name: polygon-degenerate
cases.covers: A polygon flattened onto a line. PDFium has no appearance to bake for one, so the verdict is a third thing: the edit landed and the stream could not be rebuilt. A client is told rather than shown a stale picture.

cases.name: polygon-clear-cloudy
cases.covers: A polygon is the one vertex kind with a /BE, and it clears on the same terms a shape does.

cases.name: polygon-clear-interior
cases.covers: A tri-state clear of a fill that was there. On the create path clearing and not saying are the same thing; here they are not.

cases.name: polygon-width-only
cases.covers: A border width with no style. /BS takes both in one call, so the writer has to READ the style rather than default it: defaulting would reset a dashed border nobody mentioned.

cases.name: polygon-style-only
cases.covers: The other half of the /BS read-modify-write: a style with no width. Defaulting the width would reset a three-point border nobody mentioned.

cases.name: polygon-clear-rotation
cases.covers: The rotation scalar, removed. A vertex kind carries an angle and no logical box; since 6153c181e the angle turns the upright points when the appearance is drawn, so clearing it is the whole of un-rotating one and regenerates the appearance.

cases.name: polyline-endings
cases.covers: The /LE pair, changed after creation. The two ends differ, so a writer that wrote one twice is visible.

cases.name: line-endpoints
cases.covers: Moving a line is moving its two points, and its /Rect is the caller arithmetic over them.

cases.name: ink-replace-strokes
cases.covers: A new pen path. There is no way to replace one stroke, so the whole list goes and the new one is appended; half of that leaves the old strokes under the new ones.

cases.name: text-state-alone
cases.covers: A /State with no /StateModel, which a DRAFT refuses. A patch touches what it states and the model is already on the annotation, so the rule is draft-only.

cases.name: text-clear-state
cases.covers: A tri-state clear of the review state. Removing the entry is not the same as setting it to none, which is a state a workflow can mean.

cases.name: text-icon
cases.covers: The /Name icon, changed after creation. The picture is the generator's, baked from /C and /Name.

cases.name: caret-rotate-existing-box
cases.covers: A rotation with no unrotatedRect in the patch, which a DRAFT refuses. The box is already on the annotation, so the pair is satisfied and this is what rotating a box a second time looks like.

cases.name: free-text-size-only
cases.covers: A /DA size with no font and no colour. /DA is one string, so the writer READS the other two rather than defaulting them: defaulting would reset a font nobody mentioned.

cases.name: free-text-colour-only
cases.covers: A /DA colour with no font and no size, over a text box that has both. The other two are read; defaulting them would shrink the text to twelve points and reset the family.

cases.name: free-text-clear-background
cases.covers: A tri-state clear of /C, which on a free text is the BOX BACKGROUND rather than the mark.

cases.name: redact-clear-label
cases.covers: A tri-state clear of /OverlayText. There is no call that removes the entry, so an empty string is how a label goes away.

cases.name: redact-label-colour-only
cases.covers: A label colour with no size, over a marking whose label is nine points. Unlike free text, a redaction writes /DA whole: the entry belongs to the label rather than to the annotation, so the nine points go back to twelve.

cases.name: redact-relabel
cases.covers: A new label and a new alignment on an existing marking.

cases.name: redact-more-quads
cases.covers: A text redaction gaining a region, with no rect in the patch. The box follows the quads here, unlike on a draft: a patch that moves the regions and says nothing about the box is asking for the box to follow.

cases.name: redact-quads-and-rect
cases.covers: The other branch: a patch that supplies both. It has already decided what the box is, so the quads do not get to decide again, and the margin survives.

cases.name: link-retarget
cases.covers: A link pointed somewhere else. The action is replaced rather than merged.

cases.name: link-kill-target
cases.covers: A dead link. Both /A and /Dest go, because removing only the action would resurrect a stale direct destination as the live target.

cases.name: file-attachment-icon
cases.covers: A marker restyled. The FILE is not patchable: bytes enter once, and replacing them is a different attachment.

cases.name: stamp-move-only
cases.covers: A stamp moved with no new bytes. The existing appearance is re-fitted into the new box, which is what makes moving one cheap.

cases.name: stamp-replace-source
cases.covers: New bytes. The existing appearance objects are dropped and the picture is authored again; painting over them would leave the old one underneath.

cases.name: ink-intent
cases.covers: The only /IT ink carries, set after creation.
